title: AI and the worker: BMS calls for global regulation
author: Editorial Desk
summary: At an international congress in April 2025, BMS asked governments to put guardrails around artificial intelligence.
body:
*Photo: BMS at an international congress on AI and work, April 2025*

In April 2025, the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh told an international congress that governments should set up **regulatory mechanisms for artificial intelligence (AI)**, so that workers are protected from job displacement and the gains of productivity are shared.

## The two sides of AI

AI can raise productivity, take over dangerous tasks and create new kinds of work. It can also replace jobs, intensify surveillance and put decisions about hiring, pay and discipline in the hands of algorithms that no worker can question.

## The BMS position

As reported on the BMS website, the organisation's message was that:

- governments should **regulate AI** nationally and cooperate on rules internationally,
- workers should be protected against **displacement**, and re-skilling should be a right,
- productivity gains should reach **workers** as well as owners,
- technology should be a **tool of human development**, not a replacement for human beings.

## The bigger frame

This sits well with BMS's old insistence on *Rashtra hit, Udyog hit, Mazdoor hit*. Technology is welcome when it serves all three.

## Why unions must engage

Trade unions that wait until a technology is deployed find that the decisions have already been taken. Engaging early, through consultation, collective bargaining and law, is the practical way to shape how AI enters the workplace.
